headline: Exact dense rotated matrices with nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1} and cap-one three-fragment physical laws can still satisfy p_Q(0)->3sqrt(2) while remote activity, support diameter and fourth moments all diverge.

partner_result_applied.actual_application: The partner four-region characteristic-function bounds are applied to the present exact three-interval phi_m to prove integral_{|t|>sqrt(m)} |psi_m(t)| dt -> 0; their proof is uniform in the remote center through |cos(D_m s)|<=1.

newest_claude_result_applied.actual_application: Lemma 1 with p=m on the actual cap-one fragmented f_m gives integral |psi_m| <= 4pi and hence ||h_m||_infinity <= 2; this is used in the cone-tail estimate.

proof_core: The exact row characteristic function admits the account02/B17 four-region tail bounds.
Lindeberg plus variance convergence gives pointwise Gaussian convergence; partner tails upgrade it to L1 characteristic-function convergence and uniform density convergence.
The dense rotated frame R_m satisfies R_m^T R_m=I and A_m=R_m diag(1,1,-1) R_m^T has exact nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}.
The exact null-cone coarea identity, uniform bank cap 2 and second-moment tail control give p_Qm(0)->3sqrt(2).
constraint_on_sharp_proof: A sharp proof cannot assume uniform bounded support diameter, uniformly bounded fourth moment, or finite remote-fragment activity for near-extremizers before product-bank aggregation.
unresolved: No witness above 3sqrt(2); full universal upper bound remains open. Focus next on macroscopic non-collinear/shared-coordinate heavy structures, genuinely finite or mesoscopic non-Gaussian mechanisms, coupled tails, or off-center/two-sheet effects.
